name: la6176-vocal-strip
description: The canonical LA-6176 use: a complete VOCAL channel strip in one pass — 610 preamp + 75 Hz rumble cut + a touch of 610 air + LA-2A opto leveling. This is what the hardware 6176 is famous for (Coldplay/Adele/Pharrell vocals). 610 Line preamp (clean, or +5 for a hint of warmth), cut_filter 75Hz removes proximity rumble, low shelf flat, high shelf +3 @10k for air/sheen, and the LA-2A in Comp at pk_red 4 for smooth, transparent, program-dependent level control. Reusable on any lead vocal/VO stem. (Validated to RENDER on the Watercolors drum loop; tune pk_red/air per source.)
intended_for: a lead vocal or voiceover stem that wants a single classic console-channel pass: clean tube preamp, HPF, air, and smooth opto leveling
plugin_build: uaudio_la_6176.vst3 (UADx native build — renders headless; the 'UAD LA-6176 Channel Strip.component' twin passes through, do not use it). 26 enum params; the string switches + dyn_mode + digit-prefixed 1176_* need this setattr harness.
notes: VOCAL VARIANTS: for an aggressive/up-front vocal switch dyn_mode to '1176' at 1176_ratio 4:1, 1176_input ~4, fast-ish atk (6-7) — the FET bite that sits a vocal forward. The LA-2A here is the smooth/transparent option.
cut_filter 75Hz is the proximity-rumble HPF (measured: removes low energy, raises crest, brightens). Use it on close-mic'd vocals; turn Off for sources that need their low end.

AIR without harshness: high shelf +3 @10k. If it gets sibilant, follow with [[de-ess]] (the LA-6176 has no de-esser). For presence/intelligibility instead of air, move the high band to 7k or add a low-mid body bump (low shelf 200 +1.5..+3).

If recording through an Apollo, the hardware version is Unison-enabled (impedance/gain matching) — that is an interface feature; offline here the Mic-path impedance options are tone-inert, so use Line on a recorded stem.
The harness peak-normalizes to -1 dBFS. On a real vocal, set la2a_gain for the target level instead and A/B loudness-matched.
